implementation_notes: Python already selects behaviour from the properties of the value at runtime: @functools.singledispatch turns a function into a type-to-implementation registry that dispatches on the first argument's class, follows the MRO, honours virtual subclasses registered on ABCs and falls back to the implementation registered for object, while an ABC whose __subclasshook__ checks for methods (as collections.abc does) tests a property instead of an inheritance declaration. typing.Protocol (PEP 544) is the same idea for static checkers, with @runtime_checkable giving a method-presence check at runtime. The classic descriptor is replaced by a dispatch registry plus ABCs/Protocols; write a plain dict[type, handler] only when precedence must differ from MRO order.
pitfalls: The dispatch registry is not thread-safe during registration (PEP 443 says so explicitly): register handlers at import time, never from request-handling code, and note that a later ABC.register() call invalidates the dispatch cache globally.

Dispatch uses the runtime class of the first argument only: list[int] is not a distinct runtime type, generic arguments are invisible, and a class that is a virtual subclass of two registered ABCs raises RuntimeError: Ambiguous dispatch instead of choosing one.

@runtime_checkable protocols verify only that the named methods exist - not their signatures and not their behaviour - so a partial implementation passes the property check and fails later at the call.
